topic.focus: short interest and short squeeze dynamics as equity selection signal

papers.title: Days to Cover and Stock Returns
papers.hypothesis: Long stocks ranked highest on days-to-cover (short interest divided by 20-day average volume) to harvest squeeze risk premium; DTC is orthogonal to short interest level and predicts positive return skewness.
papers.rationale: Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman, Yan (NBER w21166) show DTC captures the exit-cost of crowded shorts: high-DTC stocks are hard for short sellers to liquidate, creating squeeze potential. Unlike short interest ratio (which is bearish), high DTC predicts positive skewness and a distinct positive return premium in the cross-section. The 14-day skip accounts for the bi-monthly NASDAQ short interest reporting lag, avoiding stale data contamination.

papers.title: Surprise in Short Interest
papers.hypothesis: Long stocks with negative short interest surprise (actual SI below the cross-sectional fitted expectation) as informed short-seller withdrawal is a bullish signal that negatively predicts returns.
papers.rationale: Hanauer, Lesnevski, Smajlbegovic (Journal of Financial Markets, 2023) show that decomposing short interest into expected (from lagged beta, size, B/M, momentum cross-sectional regression) and surprise components reveals only the surprise drives returns. Negative SSIR signals unexpected short-seller retreat, a bullish catalyst. Crucially the effect is unrelated to short-selling frictions and survives in international data, suggesting it reflects genuine information rather than a limits-to-arbitrage artifact.

papers.title: The Loan Fee Anomaly: A Short Seller's Best Ideas
papers.hypothesis: Filter momentum winners by keeping only low-borrow-fee stocks (bottom quintile of equity loan fee / utilization rate) to avoid names where informed short sellers have highest conviction.
papers.rationale: Management Science 2024 paper shows equity loan fees dominate 120+ known anomalies as cross-sectional return predictors — high-fee stocks are where short sellers concentrate their best ideas and these stocks severely underperform. For a long-only momentum strategy, requiring borrow fee below the 20th percentile removes stocks with embedded short-seller conviction, improving signal purity without requiring short execution. Borrow fee data is available daily from securities lending feeds (IHS Markit, S3).

papers.title: Crowding Risk and Short Squeezes
papers.hypothesis: Long momentum stocks with high crowding scores (SI-as-pct-of-float × DTC) combined with positive recent price momentum, as squeeze dynamics amplify and extend returns when short covering is forced.
papers.rationale: Dusaniwsky (S3 Partners, EFMA 2025) documents that crowded short positions in stocks already exhibiting price strength produce squeeze dynamics that accelerate and extend momentum. Constructing a composite crowding score (SI/float × DTC) and requiring positive 63-day trailing return (confirming the squeeze catalyst is active) selects stocks where forced short covering will continue to drive prices. This is a concentrated signal but has high precision for momentum amplification.

papers.title: How Prevalent Are Short Squeezes? Evidence from the US and Europe
papers.hypothesis: Event-flag stocks where shares on loan cross above shares available to lend (utilization > 100%) and go long, as lender squeezes trigger forced covering and predict significant 5-10 day price appreciation.
papers.rationale: Allen, Haas, Pirovano, Tengulov (SSRN 4526147 / Journal of Banking & Finance 2025) provide first large-sample evidence showing lender squeezes (loan > supply, utilization > 100%) produce measurable positive abnormal returns as short sellers are forced to cover. The event affects ~10% of US stocks per quarter, is short-lived (5-10 days), and is distinct from voluntary squeeze dynamics. As a daily event signal layered onto momentum ranking, this identifies stocks with an immediate mechanical catalyst for price appreciation.
